pretraining_revision: Original two-scene preflight retained: direct cropped-graph steering caused severe wall contact. Before any pilot training or validation, use frozen measured-memory nominal control; graph-following remains an explicit candidate. Noisy local attachment is not assumed globally correct.
pretraining_fairness_revision: Before pilot training, give the matched classical TPG controller a measured retreat rule when its waiting position obstructs a predecessor. Both learned and classical high decisions respect identical nonpreemption masks. Preserve V1/V2 preflight artifacts.
sensor_freshness_revision: First pilot interrupted before validation after code audit: reservation release must require fresh detection and geometry for BOTH agents; low auxiliary labels also require per-agent new measurements. Preserve interrupted source, completed checkpoints and partial attempts; rerun all arms from scratch under the corrected source, without using first-run training outcomes to select a model.
hypothesis: Measured local 3D route reservations with event-triggered learned priority, plus a causal learned low-level residual controller, can reduce coordination burden without hiding safety or efficacy regressions.
observation_contract: command_aligned_local_geometry_v1; only the same measured crops, tracks, noisy preoperative targets and requested-command history for all arms
fairness: Same fixed initial scenes, same sensor stream configuration, measured graph and safety layer. Old balanced_1s stays as an additional historical-surface strong comparator. Graph-only, high-only, low-only, both and untrained are separately reported.
selection: All three seeds and all requested attempts retained; no best-seed selection; no confirmation access. Pilot is development evidence only.
claims: Rolling local TPG prototype, not full robust MAPF or a safety certificate. Unknown route length stays unknown. Euclidean spacing is not calibrated magnetic independence. Neither upper nor lower learning novelty or superiority is presumed.
